articles.title: 2002 Udupi murder accused, associate of Kali Yogish, brought back from UAE
articles.summary: Udupi: The CBI, in coordination with the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and Karnataka Police, has secured the deportation of red notice accused Rajesh Keshava Acharya, an associate of underworld fugitive Kali Yogish, from the UAE to India. Acharya arrived in Mumbai on Friday, where he was taken into custody by the Karnataka Police. CBI SECURES DEPORTATION OF WANTED FUGITIVE RAJESH KESHAVA ACHARYA FROM UAE pic.twitter.com/jPYyK0aHWh — Central Bureau of Investigation (India) (@CBIHeadquarters) November 27, 2026 He was wanted in connection with a murder case registered by the Udupi Town police. Acharya was wanted for his alleged role in the murder of Manohar Shetty on July 18, 2002. On July 17, 2002, Acharya conspired with three other accused, Vinod Shettigar, Dinesh alias Lefty Dinesh and Gopinath, to murder Manohar Shetty. On July 18, 2002, Shetty was attacked and killed near Kukkikatte Junction by Vinod and Dinesh. Acharya fled India in 2019. A chargesheet in the case has already been filed before the court against all the accused, including Acharya. At the request of Karnataka Police, NCB-New Delhi issued a Red Notice against Acharya through Interpol channels. Key accused in Chhattisgarh liquor scam brought back from UAE He was arrested by UAE authorities and, following the completion of legal formalities, extradited to India. A CBI release said that, as the National Central Bureau (NCB) for Interpol in India, it coordinates with law enforcement agencies across the country through Bharatpol to facilitate international police cooperation. articles.title: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri in another case; bacteria found in Bengal sample
articles.summary: New Delhi: Food regulator FSSAI has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after a packaged drinking water sample collected from its West Bengal plant failed laboratory testing, sources said. The sample tested positive for coliform bacteria, they added. This form of bacteria can enter water systems through sewage leaks or damaged pipes, among other pathways. This action marks the second instance of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) sanctioning prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd, a leading player in the packaged drinking water sector in the country. On Sunday, the FSSAI announced similar legal proceedings after a sample from one of Bisleri's plants in Goa also failed testing. The West Bengal sample was taken from a plant in Jalpaiguri's Telipara village. The presence of coliform bacteria was confirmed by both primary and referral laboratories. As a result, the FSSAI prohibited the sale of only one specific batch (batch number PB 201) on August 12, 2026, sources stated. Food labelling: ‘FSSAI should use science-based nutrient thresholds’, say public health campaigners In view of the violations of the food safety rules, FSSAI has granted "sanction for prosecution" against Bisleri International. Responses from the FSSAI and Bisleri International could not be ascertained immediately. In the Goa case, the FSSAI had said the "sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006." Following an appeal from Bisleri, the sample was forwarded to a referral food laboratory, which also classified it as "unsafe" due to detection of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), according to the regulator. These laboratory findings confirmed violations related to unsafe food practices, which led the FSSAI to initiate prosecution under the Food Safety Act, 2006. On Monday, Bisleri International asserted that its product is safe for consumption and that the company would cooperate with the FSSAI to address the issues raised. Earlier this week, FSSAI CEO Rajit Punhani stated that the agency is collecting packaged drinking water samples nationwide, with lab testing for quality expected to be completed within one to two months. He emphasised that enforcement actions aim to ensure compliance, not to create panic. He noted that the regulator, in the past year, has undertaken enforcement activities for many food as well as beverage products, adding that it would soon start inspection of 'packaging materials' used for food items. Additionally, the FSSAI has expanded the scope of its scrutiny. The central regulator has communicated with state food commissioners and regional directors to enhance surveillance, inspection, and sampling of 'packaged drinking water and mineral water.' It also asked them to take action against companies in case of non-compliance. In this calendar year, the FSSAI has increased enforcement measures against food business operators and e-commerce companies. The regulator has also taken action against manufacturers of energy drinks and alcoholic beverages.

A team of Chhattisgarh Police travelled to the UAE to take custody of Agrawal at the Dubai International Airport. It arrived at the Mumbai airport on Friday, the CBI said.
